solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Presumption each end of the year holds value

indicators.note: both ends of a word are its first and last letters, so only those two are kept
something that holds another thing wraps around it, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: the first and last letters of 'the'
Y is the standard abbreviation for year
merit is worth or value

explanation.surface: Someone assumes that the close of each year will hold its worth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'each end of the year' reads as one phrase about the calendar, but 'each end of' applies only to the little word 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: Temerity is reckless boldness, a close synonym of presumption or audacity.

clue.text: Swapping elements of scheme gets communication, of course

indicators.note: exchanging the two halves of a word moves its front part round to the back

blocks.note: a tactic is a scheme or plan

explanation.surface: Rearranging the parts of a plan produces a message along the way.
explanation.walkthrough: TACTIC splits neatly into TAC and TIC; swap them. 'Of course' means on the racecourse, where tic-tac is the hand-signalling bookmakers use to pass on odds.
explanation.definitionFit: Tic-tac is the sign language British racecourse bookies use to communicate betting odds to each other.

clue.text: Take advantage of some drinks in hiring programme

blocks.note: to milk a situation is to exploit it
a round is a set of drinks bought for a group

explanation.surface: Someone exploits a few drinks during a recruitment drive.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the milk round is the annual tour of universities by employers recruiting graduates, named after the milkman's daily delivery route.
explanation.definitionFit: The milk round is the yearly graduate recruitment campaign that big employers run at British universities.

clue.text: Regret pig fat is said to be in this dish

indicators.note: something said is spoken out loud, so we go by how the words sound rather than how they are spelt

blocks.note: rue is to regret and lard is pig fat; spoken together they match the dish

explanation.surface: A diner laments the pork fat that supposedly went into the meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A roulade is a rolled dish, meat or sponge spread with a filling and rolled up.

clue.text: Cat flap extremely busy

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only its first and last letters are used

blocks.note: a tab is a small flap
the first and last letters of 'busy'

explanation.surface: The cat flap is getting a great deal of traffic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cat flap' reads as one thing, but the definition stops at 'Cat'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tabby is a cat with a striped or mottled coat, so it is one kind of cat.

clue.text: Stand or stumble: too many drugs?

blocks.note: to trip is to stumble
OD is short for overdose, taking too many drugs

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a person can stay upright or will fall after overdoing the drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: A tripod is a three-legged stand, used to hold a camera steady.

clue.text: Very left-wing cardinal Vatican finally drops in reshuffle

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word before it
to drop something is to let it fall away, so that letter leaves the word
a reshuffle deals the letters out again in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
the last letter of 'Vatican'

explanation.surface: A firebrand cardinal is dropped when the Vatican reshuffles its senior posts.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the N out of CARDINAL, then rearrange what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Radical politics seeks fundamental change, so a radical is strongly left-wing.

clue.text: Phoney subscription raised under pressure

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a word makes it read from the bottom upwards
in a down entry, a piece that sits under another is written after it

blocks.note: P is the symbol for pressure
dues are a membership subscription

explanation.surface: A bogus membership fee was hiked when somebody was put under pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: A pseud is a pretentious person faking intellect or taste, a British slang word for a phoney.

clue.text: Regularly idle, joined the army — just

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

blocks.note: the second and fourth letters of 'idle'
to serve in the army is to have joined up

explanation.surface: Someone often lazy simply went into the army.
explanation.walkthrough: 'just' looks like the adverb 'only', but here it is the adjective meaning fair.
explanation.definitionFit: A just reward is one that is merited, earned, fairly due.

clue.text: Very stupid to conceal internet supplier issue

indicators.note: to conceal something is to hide it inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: dense means slow-witted
ISP stands for internet service provider

explanation.surface: It was foolish of an internet company to hide a problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'issue' looks like a noun meaning problem; it is the verb meaning hand out.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispense is to give out or distribute, as one issues supplies.

clue.text: Seeing problem, new counsellor bids for resolution

indicators.note: a resolution works the letters out into a settled new form

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for new
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A problem arises when a new counsellor tries to resolve something.
explanation.definitionFit: Colour blindness is a defect of vision, an inability to tell certain colours apart.

clue.text: Pitch right into a clue, beginning to yield so soon?

indicators.note: to pitch is to throw, here to toss one letter into the middle of the phrase that follows
the beginning of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: taken as written
a lead is a clue in an investigation
R is the abbreviation for right
the first letter of 'yield'

explanation.surface: A setter wonders whether to throw the right clue in, then gives up remarkably quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pitch' looks like a noun but is the verb meaning throw; R goes into A LEAD after its L, then Y follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Already means sooner than expected, the surprised question 'so soon?' in one word.

clue.text: Choose a way in to catch fighter in the ring

indicators.note: to catch words is to hear them, so it is the sound that counts

blocks.note: pick is choose and a door is a way in; said together they match the fighter

explanation.surface: Someone selects an entrance in order to trap a boxer.
explanation.walkthrough: The ring is the bullring, not a boxing ring.
explanation.definitionFit: A picador is the horseman in a bullfight who goads the bull with a lance.

clue.text: Silences pale, white creature

blocks.note: mutes is a verb meaning silences
wan means pale

explanation.surface: A pale, white creature is struck silent.
explanation.definitionFit: The mute swan is the common all-white swan of Britain and Europe.

clue.text: Exhausted, did domestic chore

blocks.note: first meaning: finished, spent, no longer of use
second meaning: cleaned the dishes after a meal

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one tired person after the housework; the two parts are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A washed-up person is finished and spent, while washing up is the British phrase for doing the dishes.

clue.text: Left part of church, one's faith having done this?

definitions.note: the definition describes what faith does when someone stops practising a religion

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for left
the apse is the domed recess at the end of a church

explanation.surface: A churchgoer walked out of part of the church, faith apparently gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' looks like the past tense of leave; it is the abbreviation L. A lapsed Catholic is one whose faith has fallen away.
explanation.definitionFit: Faith that lapses falls into disuse, the way a believer stops attending and practising.

clue.text: Purchaser's first to rave about old flat

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of the word is used
about means going around, so one piece wraps another

blocks.note: the first letter of 'Purchaser'
to enthuse is to rave about something
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A buyer is the first to gush over a period apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flat' is the noun for an apartment, not the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A penthouse is a luxury flat on the top floor of a building.

clue.text: Alliance dispersed a mob

indicators.note: dispersed means scattered, so the letters are spread out into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An alliance broke up and a crowd was scattered.
explanation.definitionFit: Canaille, from French, is a contemptuous word for the rabble or common crowd.

clue.text: Make sense of commercial by party

indicators.note: by means next to, so one piece is placed straight after the other

blocks.note: an ad is a commercial
the DUP is the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: Someone tries to understand an advertisement put out by a political party.
explanation.definitionFit: If things add up they are consistent and make sense.

clue.text: Quietly made a bow, desperate for a drink

blocks.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quietly
to arch is to curve into a bow shape

explanation.surface: A performer bowed silently, gasping for something to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made a bow' suggests a curtsey or greeting; it means bent into a curve.
explanation.definitionFit: Parched means extremely dry or thirsty.

clue.text: General having succeeded showing signs of distress

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for succeeded, used in family trees
weeping is crying, a sign of distress

explanation.surface: A military commander, after a victory, is seen in tears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'General' looks like an army officer; it is the adjective meaning broad.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweeping statements are broad and wide-ranging, the same as general ones.

clue.text: Bowl with a revolutionary swagger

blocks.note: a pan is a bowl-shaped vessel
taken as written
Che Guevara is the archetypal revolutionary

explanation.surface: A revolutionary walks with a strut, or someone bowls with style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bowl' may suggest the cricket verb; it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Panache is flamboyant confidence and style, close in sense to swagger.

clue.text: Attend the event, or buzz off

blocks.note: first meaning: split into three words, be present at it
second meaning: go away

explanation.walkthrough: The first meaning reads the answer as three words, BE AT IT; the second is the slang order to leave.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Beat it!' is a slang command to go away, just like 'buzz off'.

clue.text: Inn opening time: taxi!

indicators.note: opening up a word splits it apart so that something can be placed inside

blocks.note: an age is a long period of time
Uber is the ride-hailing taxi service

explanation.surface: At an inn's opening hour someone calls for a cab.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opening time' looks like a pub's opening hour; in fact the taxi opens up the time.
explanation.definitionFit: An auberge is a French inn, a word also used in English for such a place.

clue.text: Remarks on jacket having a smear on top of buttonhole

indicators.note: in a down entry, a piece placed on another sits above it, so it comes first
the top of a word in a down entry is its first letter

blocks.note: a blur is a smudge or smear
the first letter of 'buttonhole'

explanation.surface: Someone comments on a jacket with a stain above the buttonhole.
explanation.walkthrough: The jacket is a book's dust jacket, not clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A blurb is the short promotional text printed on a book's dust jacket.

clue.text: Her wailing has been terrible

indicators.note: something terrible is in a dreadful state, so these letters are knocked into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A complaint that a woman's crying has been awful.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer while the last three words also supply the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: In Irish folklore a banshee is a female spirit whose dreadful wailing foretells a death.

clue.text: Be around where many animals are brought up to drink a lot

indicators.note: in a down entry, bringing something up makes it read from the bottom upwards
around means going about the outside, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: taken as written
a zoo is where many animals are kept

explanation.surface: A farm instruction about where animals are raised and given plenty to drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To booze is an informal verb for drinking alcohol heavily.

clue.text: Peremptorily dismiss joke: why is service bad?

blocks.note: a laugh is a joke, as in 'just for a laugh'
in tennis a serve is a fault when it lands beyond the lines

explanation.surface: Someone brushes aside a joke while asking why the service is poor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'service' suggests a restaurant; it is the tennis serve, which is bad when it lands out of court.
explanation.definitionFit: To laugh something out of court is to dismiss it scornfully as not worth considering.

clue.text: Incorporate firm at last in European group

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the word before it
in means placed inside, so this letter goes within the other pieces

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for European
a body is an organised group
the last letter of 'firm'

explanation.surface: A company has finally joined a European organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: To embody is to include or contain something as a part of a whole.

clue.text: Pious saint avoiding contrary scripture

indicators.note: avoiding something means keeping clear of it, so that letter is left out

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for saint
the reverse is the contrary or opposite
NT is the New Testament

explanation.surface: A devout saint steers clear of heretical writings.
explanation.walkthrough: REVERSE without its S gives REVERE.
explanation.definitionFit: Reverent means showing deep religious respect, which is what pious describes.
